fields.quoted_span:
No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a 
lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause.
fields.note: The core good-cause rule, the list of causes, the Notice to Quit rules, the court-judgment requirement, the ban on self-help eviction, 6x relocation, the treble damages and $10,000 penalty, and the rooming house rules are all in the document. Several details are off. The owner-occupied holdover periods differ slightly: the guide says 1 month for "other types of tenancies" as well as month-to-month. The 3-day notice for owner-occupied cases is omitted. The 5-year reuse rule applies to board-up, demolition or retirement. The owner-occupancy misuse remedy, stated as treble damages, comes with a 6-month occupancy requirement that the requirement field does not mention. The requirement's list of causes also omits public-housing lease breach, and the 18-month period applies only to retirement.

fields.quoted_span:
A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three months before filing a suit 
for eviction.
fields.note: The notice periods match the document: 3 days for disorderly conduct, damage, employment and criminal causes; 1 month for rules, lease breach, rent increase, lease changes and late payment; 2 months for post-conversion occupancy; 3 months for health and safety; 18 months for retirement; 3 years for conversion; 6x monthly rent relocation for illegal occupancy. The 3-month and 3-year periods are correct, but the value is a compressed summary that omits the cause-specific caveats.
The rule's effective_date is null, and the document states no effective date for the Anti-Eviction Act.

fields.quoted_span:
The Anti-Eviction Act,  N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1 to 61.12, was created to protect 
blameless tenants from eviction and was adopted in recognition of the housing shortage in 
the State.
fields.note: The guide presents the Act as current law that applies and is enforced. It does not use the words "in force", so the in_force status is inferred from the present-tense description.

fields.quoted_span:
The Anti-Eviction Act applies to most residential rental properties including single-family 
homes, mobile homes and land in a mobile home park, apartment buildings, and complexes. This 
law also applies to rooming and boarding homes
fields.note: The summary, the hotel/motel exemption, the trust exemption, and the owner-occupied limits are all supported. The Exceptions paragraph, however, is ambiguous and says the law "may not apply" to certain owner-occupied premises. The coverage field instead treats those premises as subject to a narrower list of causes, which the document's owner-occupied section supports.
